title.zh: 卷一百四十四 列傳第三十一: 答里麻 月魯帖木兒 卜顏鐵木兒 星吉 福壽 道童
title.en: Volume 144 Biographies 31: Dalima, Yuelutiemuer, Buyantiemuer, Xingji, Fushou, Daotong
title.raw: 卷一百四十四 列傳第三十一: 答里麻 月魯帖木兒 卜顏鐵木兒 星吉 福壽 道童 Volume 144 Biographies 31: Dalima, Yuelutiemuer, Buyantiemuer, Xingji, Fushou, Daotong

sentences.zh: 答里麻

translations.literal: Dalima
translations.idiomatic: Dalima

sentences.zh: 答里麻，高昌人。

translations.literal: Dalima was a man of Gaochang.
translations.idiomatic: Dalima was a native of Gaochang.

sentences.zh: 大父撒吉斯，为辽王傅，世祖称其贤。

translations.literal: His grandfather Sagisi served as tutor to the Prince of Liao; Shizu praised his worth.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Sagisi had been tutor to the Prince of Liao, and Kublai had praised his virtue.

sentences.zh: 从讨李璮，以勋授山东行省大都督。

translations.literal: He followed in the campaign against Li Tan and, for merit, was appointed Grand Commander of the Shandong Branch Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: He took part in the suppression of Li Tan and, for his service, was made grand commander of the Shandong Branch Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 答里麻弱冠入宿卫。

translations.literal: Dalima entered the palace guard in his early twenties.
translations.idiomatic: Dalima joined the imperial guard while still a young man.

sentences.zh: 大德十一年，授御药院达鲁花赤，迁回回药物院，寻出佥湖北、山南两道廉访司事，召拜监察御史。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year of Dade he was appointed darughachi of the Imperial Pharmacy Directorate, transferred to the Directorate of Muslim Medicines, then sent out as concurrent surveillance commissioner for the Hubei and Shannan circuits, and summoned to be investigating censor.
translations.idiomatic: In 1307 he was made darughachi of the Imperial Pharmacy Directorate, then moved to the Muslim Medicines Directorate; shortly afterward he was posted to oversee both the Hubei and Shannan surveillance commissions and was summoned to serve as an investigating censor.

sentences.zh: 时丞相帖木迭兒专权贪肆，答里麻帅同寅亦怜真、马祖常劾其罪。

translations.literal: At the time the chief councillor Temuder monopolized power and was greedy and lawless; Dalima led his colleagues Yilianzhen and Ma Zuchang in impeaching his crimes.
translations.idiomatic: The chief councillor Temuder was then monopolizing power and enriching himself by every means; Dalima joined his colleagues Yilianzhen and Ma Zuchang in impeaching him.

sentences.zh: 高昌僧恃丞相威，违法娶妇南城，答里麻诘问之，奋不顾利害，风纪由是大振。

translations.literal: A Gaochang monk, relying on the chief councillor's power, unlawfully took a wife in the southern city; Dalima interrogated him, heedless of gain or harm, and standards of conduct were thereby greatly raised.
translations.idiomatic: A monk from Gaochang, counting on the chief councillor's backing, illegally took a wife in the southern capital; Dalima questioned him without regard for his own safety, and official discipline was greatly strengthened as a result.

sentences.zh: 擢河东道廉访副使。

translations.literal: He was promoted to deputy surveillance commissioner of the Hedong Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to deputy surveillance commissioner for the Hedong circuit.

sentences.zh: 隰州村民赛神，因醉殴杀姚甲，为首者乘闹逃去，有司逮同会者系狱，历岁不决。

translations.literal: Villagers in Xi Prefecture were holding a festival to a god; in drunken brawling they beat and killed Yao Jia; the ringleader fled amid the uproar; the authorities arrested those who had been present together and imprisoned them, and for years the case was not resolved.
translations.idiomatic: At a village sacrifice in Xi Prefecture, men fighting while drunk killed Yao Jia; the leader escaped in the confusion, and the authorities jailed everyone who had been at the gathering. The case dragged on unresolved for years.

sentences.zh: 答里麻曰：「杀人者既逃，存亡不可知，此辈皆诖误无罪，而反桎梏耶？

translations.literal: Dalima said: "The killer has already fled, and whether he lives or dies is unknown; these people are all implicated by mistake and are without guilt—why should they instead be shackled?"
translations.idiomatic: Dalima said, "The murderer has fled, and we do not even know whether he is alive or dead. These men were caught up in the affair by mistake and are innocent—why keep them in chains?"

sentences.zh: 」悉纵之。

translations.literal: " He released them all.
translations.idiomatic: He released them all.

sentences.zh: 至治元年，帖木迭兒复相，以复仇为事，答里麻辞去。

translations.literal: In the first year of Zhizhi, Temuder again became chief councillor and made revenge his business; Dalima resigned.
translations.idiomatic: In 1321 Temuder returned as chief councillor and set about settling scores; Dalima resigned his post.

sentences.zh: 明年，改燕南道廉访副使。

translations.literal: The next year he was transferred to deputy surveillance commissioner of the Yannan Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he was made deputy surveillance commissioner for the Yannan circuit.

sentences.zh: 开州达鲁花赤石不花歹颇著政绩，同僚忌之，嗾民诬其与民妻俞氏饮。

translations.literal: The Kai Prefecture darughachi Shibuhuadai had achieved notable administrative results; colleagues envied him and incited the people to accuse him of drinking with a commoner's wife, Lady Yu.
translations.idiomatic: Shibuhuadai, darughachi of Kai Prefecture, had a strong record in office; jealous colleagues stirred up a charge that he had been drinking with a commoner's wife, Lady Yu.

sentences.zh: 答里麻察知俞氏乃八十老妪，石不花歹实不与饮酒，于是抵诬告者罪，石不花歹复还职。

translations.literal: Dalima investigated and learned that Lady Yu was an old woman of eighty and that Shibuhuadai had in fact not drunk with her; he therefore punished the false accusers, and Shibuhuadai was restored to office.
translations.idiomatic: Dalima found that Lady Yu was an eighty-year-old woman and that Shibuhuadai had never drunk with her; he punished the accusers for perjury and restored Shibuhuadai to his post.

sentences.zh: 行唐县民斫桑道侧，偶有人借斧削其杖，其人夜持杖劫民财，事觉，并逮斧主与盗同下狱。

translations.literal: A man in Xingtang County was cutting mulberry beside the road; someone happened to borrow his axe to trim a staff; that man took the staff by night and robbed a villager of property; when the matter came to light, both the owner of the axe and the robber were arrested and imprisoned together.
translations.idiomatic: A man in Xingtang County was trimming mulberry by the roadside when another man borrowed his axe to shape a walking staff. That night the borrower used the staff to rob a villager; when the crime was discovered, both the axe owner and the thief were thrown into prison.

sentences.zh: 答里麻原其未尝知情，即纵之。

translations.literal: Dalima excused him on the ground that he had never known of the matter and at once released him.
translations.idiomatic: Dalima ruled that the axe owner had known nothing of the crime and released him at once.

sentences.zh: 深州民媪怒殴兒妇死，妇方抱其子，子亦误触死。

translations.literal: An old woman in Shen Prefecture in anger beat her daughter-in-law to death; the daughter-in-law was holding her child, and the child also died from accidental contact.
translations.idiomatic: In Shen Prefecture an old woman beat her daughter-in-law to death in a fit of rage; the daughter-in-law was holding her infant, and the child died as well in the struggle.

sentences.zh: 媪年七十，同僚议免刑，答里麻不可，曰：「国制，罪人七十免刑，为其血气已衰，不任刑也。

translations.literal: The old woman was seventy; colleagues discussed exempting her from punishment, but Dalima would not agree, saying: "By national law, criminals seventy years old are exempted from punishment because their vital force is already weakened and they cannot bear punishment."
translations.idiomatic: The woman was seventy, and his colleagues urged that she be spared punishment, but Dalima refused, saying, "The law exempts offenders at seventy because their strength is spent and they can no longer endure punishment."

sentences.zh: 媪既能杀二人，何谓衰老？

translations.literal: This old woman was able to kill two people—how can one speak of weakness from age?
translations.idiomatic: Yet this woman killed two people—how can we call her too feeble to punish?"

sentences.zh: 」卒死狱中。

translations.literal: " In the end she died in prison.
translations.idiomatic: She died in prison.

sentences.zh: 至治元年，除济宁路总管，兴学劝农，百废具修，府无停事。

translations.literal: In the first year of Zhizhi he was appointed prefect of Jining Circuit; he promoted schools and encouraged agriculture, every neglected matter was put in order, and the prefecture had no backlog of business.
translations.idiomatic: In 1321 he was appointed prefect of Jining; he revived schools, encouraged farming, and put every neglected office in order so that no case lay idle in the prefectural yamen.

sentences.zh: 济阳县有牧童持铁连结击野雀，误杀同牧者，系狱数岁。

translations.literal: In Jiyang County a shepherd boy, swinging an iron chain to strike wild sparrows, by mistake killed a fellow shepherd and was imprisoned for several years.
translations.idiomatic: In Jiyang County a shepherd boy swinging an iron chain at sparrows accidentally killed another boy tending the flock and was kept in prison for years.

sentences.zh: 答里麻曰：「小兒误杀同牧者，实无杀人意，难以定罪。

translations.literal: Dalima said: "A small child who by mistake killed a fellow shepherd in fact had no intent to kill; it is hard to convict him."
translations.idiomatic: Dalima said, "This was a child who killed another child by accident; he had no intent to murder, and a capital conviction cannot stand."

sentences.zh: 」罚铜遣之。

translations.literal: " He fined him in copper and sent him away.
translations.idiomatic: He imposed a fine in copper and released the boy.

sentences.zh: 泰定元年，升福建廉访使。

translations.literal: In the first year of Taiding he was promoted to surveillance commissioner of Fujian.
translations.idiomatic: In 1324 he was promoted to surveillance commissioner of Fujian.

sentences.zh: 朝廷遣宦官伯颜催督绣段，横取民财，宣政院判官术邻亦取赂于富僧，答里麻皆劾之。

translations.literal: The court sent the eunuch Boyan to press for delivery of embroidered silks and he extorted the people's wealth; the Xuanzheng Yuan judge Shulin also took bribes from wealthy monks; Dalima impeached them all.
translations.idiomatic: The court had sent the eunuch Boyan to hurry production of embroidered silks, and he extorted money from the people; Shulin, a judge of the Xuanzheng Yuan, also took bribes from rich monks—Dalima impeached them both.

sentences.zh: 迁浙西廉访使。

translations.literal: He was transferred to surveillance commissioner of Zhexi.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to surveillance commissioner of western Zhejiang.

sentences.zh: 会文宗发江陵，阿兒哈秃来谕旨，求赂不获，还谮于朝，召至京，处以重罪。

translations.literal: When Wenzong set out from Jiangling, Aerhatu came to convey an edict; Dalima would not give a bribe; on returning he slandered him at court; Dalima was summoned to the capital and sentenced to a heavy penalty.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wenzong marched out from Jiangling, Aerhatu came bearing an edict; Dalima refused his demand for a bribe, and Aerhatu slandered him at court on his return. Dalima was summoned to the capital and condemned to a heavy punishment.

sentences.zh: 比至，帝怒解，迁上都同知留守。

translations.literal: When he arrived, the emperor's anger was dispelled, and he was transferred to associate intendant of the Shangdu garrison.
translations.idiomatic: By the time he reached the capital the emperor's anger had passed, and he was appointed associate intendant at Shangdu.

sentences.zh: 天历二年八月，明宗崩，文宗入正大统，使者旁午。

translations.literal: In the eighth month of the second year of Tianli, Mingzong died; Wenzong entered to take the great succession, and envoys came and went without pause.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month of 1329 Emperor Mingzong died and Wenzong assumed the throne; messengers shuttled back and forth without cease.

sentences.zh: 答里麻朝暮尽力，事无缺失，帝特赐锦衣以嘉之。

translations.literal: Dalima exerted himself morning and evening; nothing was left undone; the emperor specially bestowed brocade robes to commend him.
translations.idiomatic: Dalima labored from dawn to dusk until nothing was left undone; the emperor rewarded him with a suit of brocade robes.

sentences.zh: 天历三年，迁淮东廉访使。

translations.literal: In the third year of Tianli he was transferred to surveillance commissioner of Huaidong.
translations.idiomatic: In 1330 he was made surveillance commissioner of eastern Huai.

sentences.zh: 明年，召拜刑部尚书。

translations.literal: The next year he was summoned and appointed minister of justice.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he was summoned to serve as minister of justice.

sentences.zh: 国制，新君即位，必赐诸王、驸马、妃主及宿卫官吏金帛。

translations.literal: By national regulation, when a new ruler acceded he must bestow gold and silks on princes, imperial sons-in-law, consorts and princesses, and palace-guard officials.
translations.idiomatic: By court custom, a new emperor's accession required gifts of gold and silk for princes, imperial sons-in-law, consorts, princesses, and the palace guard.

sentences.zh: 答里麻曰：「必唱名给散，无虚增之数。

translations.literal: Dalima said: "Names must be called out when distributing; there must be no fictitious increase in numbers."
translations.idiomatic: Dalima insisted that gifts be handed out only when each recipient's name was called, with no padded rolls on the lists.

sentences.zh: 」国费大省，帝复赐黄金腰带以旌其能。

translations.literal: " State expenses were greatly reduced; the emperor again bestowed a golden belt to honor his ability.
translations.idiomatic: State expenditure fell sharply, and the emperor again rewarded him with a golden belt.

sentences.zh: 元统元年，升辽阳行省参知政事。

translations.literal: In the first year of Yuantong he was promoted to vice administrator of the Liaoyang Branch Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: In 1333 he was promoted to vice administrator of the Liaoyang Branch Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 高丽国使朝京，道过辽阳，谒省官，各奉布四匹、书一幅，用征东省印封之。

translations.literal: Envoys of Goryeo came to court in the capital; passing through Liaoyang they called on the provincial officials, each presenting four bolts of cloth and one letter, sealed with the seal of the Eastern Campaign Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Envoys from Goryeo on their way to court called at Liaoyang and presented each provincial officer with four bolts of cloth and a letter sealed with the Eastern Campaign Secretariat's stamp.

sentences.zh: 答里麻诘其使曰：「国制，设印以署公牍、防奸伪，何为封私书？

translations.literal: Dalima questioned the envoy, saying: "By national regulation, seals are established to affix to public documents and guard against fraud—why seal a private letter?"
translations.idiomatic: Dalima challenged the envoy: "Seals exist to authenticate public documents and prevent fraud—why use one on a private letter?"

sentences.zh: 况汝出国时，我尚在京，未为辽阳省官，今何故有书遗我？

translations.literal: Moreover, when you left your country I was still in the capital and was not yet an official of the Liaoyang secretariat—why now is there a letter left for me?
translations.idiomatic: When you left home I was still in the capital and held no post in Liaoyang—why address a letter to me now?"

sentences.zh: 汝君臣何欺诈如是耶？

translations.literal: Why are your ruler and ministers so deceitful as this?
translations.idiomatic: What sort of trickery is this from your king and his ministers?"

sentences.zh: 」使辞屈，还其书与布。

translations.literal: " The envoy had no reply and returned the letter and cloth.
translations.idiomatic: The envoy could not answer and took back the letter and cloth.

sentences.zh: 元统三年，迁山东廉访使。

translations.literal: In the third year of Yuantong he was transferred to surveillance commissioner of Shandong.
translations.idiomatic: In 1335 he was transferred to surveillance commissioner of Shandong.

sentences.zh: 时山东盗起，陈马骡及新李白昼杀掠。

translations.literal: At the time bandits arose in Shandong; Chen Maluo and Xin Bai plundered and killed by day.
translations.idiomatic: Banditry had broken out in Shandong; Chen Maluo and Xin Bai were raiding and killing in broad daylight.

sentences.zh: 答里麻以为官吏贪污所致，先劾去之而后上擒贼方略。

translations.literal: Dalima held that this was caused by officials' corruption; he first impeached and removed them, then submitted a plan for capturing the bandits.
translations.idiomatic: Dalima blamed corrupt officials for the disorder; he impeached and removed them first, then submitted a plan to capture the bandits.

sentences.zh: 朝廷嘉纳之，即遣兵擒获，齐鲁以安。

translations.literal: The court praised and accepted it, immediately sent troops to capture them, and Qi and Lu were thereby pacified.
translations.idiomatic: The court approved his plan, sent troops at once, and captured the leaders, bringing peace back to Shandong.

sentences.zh: 除大都路留守。

translations.literal: He was appointed intendant of the Dadu Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed intendant of the Dadu metropolitan district.

sentences.zh: 帝宴大臣于延春阁，特赐答里麻白鹰以表其贞廉。

translations.literal: The emperor feasted his ministers in the Yanchun Pavilion and specially bestowed on Dalima a white hawk to mark his integrity.
translations.idiomatic: At a feast for his ministers in the Yanchun Pavilion, the emperor gave Dalima a white hawk as a token of his incorruptibility.

sentences.zh: 帝尝命答里麻修七星堂，先是，修缮必用赤绿金银装饰，答里麻独务朴素，令画工图山林景物，左右年少皆不然。

translations.literal: The emperor once ordered Dalima to repair the Seven Stars Hall; previously repairs always used red, green, gold, and silver ornament; Dalima alone pursued simplicity and had painters depict mountain forests and scenery; the young attendants on left and right all disapproved.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor once put Dalima in charge of restoring the Seven Stars Hall, where past work had always been done in gilded colors and precious metals; Dalima insisted on simplicity and had the painters depict mountain landscapes instead, to the dismay of the younger courtiers around him.

sentences.zh: 是岁秋，车驾自上京还，入观之，乃大喜，以手抚壁叹曰：「有心哉，留守也！

translations.literal: That autumn, when the imperial carriage returned from Shangdu and he entered to view it, he was greatly pleased, stroked the wall with his hand, and sighed: "What care the intendant has shown!"
translations.idiomatic: That autumn, when the emperor returned from Shangdu and entered the hall, he was delighted; stroking the wall he exclaimed, "This intendant has a true heart!"

sentences.zh: 」赐白金五十两、锦衣一袭。

translations.literal: " He bestowed fifty taels of white gold and one suit of brocade robes.
translations.idiomatic: He rewarded him with fifty taels of silver and a suit of brocade robes.

sentences.zh: 至正六年，升河南行省右丞，改翰林学士承旨。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Zhizheng he was promoted to right vice administrator of the Henan Branch Secretariat, then changed to academician-expositor of the Hanlin Academy.
translations.idiomatic: In 1346 he was made right vice administrator of the Henan Branch Secretariat, then transferred to expositor-in-chief of the Hanlin Academy.

sentences.zh: 至正七年，迁陕西行台中丞，时年六十九。

translations.literal: In the seventh year of Zhizheng he was transferred to vice censor-in-chief of the Shaanxi Branch Censorate; he was then sixty-nine.
translations.idiomatic: In 1347 he was moved to vice censor-in-chief of the Shaanxi Branch Censorate, at the age of sixty-nine.

sentences.zh: 致事后，召商议中书平章政事，不拜，全俸优养终身。

translations.literal: After he retired from office, he was summoned to deliberate as grand councillor of the Central Secretariat but did not accept; he received his full salary in generous maintenance for life.
translations.idiomatic: After retirement he was summoned to serve as grand councillor of the Central Secretariat but declined; he was granted his full salary in honorable maintenance for the rest of his life.

sentences.zh: 月鲁帖木兒

translations.literal: Yuelutiemuer
translations.idiomatic: Yuelutiemuer

sentences.zh: 月鲁帖木兒，卜领勤多礼伯台氏。

translations.literal: Yuelutiemuer was of the Bolingqinduolibotai clan.
translations.idiomatic: Yuelutiemuer belonged to the Bolingqinduolibotai clan.

sentences.zh: 曾祖贵裕，事太祖，为管领怯怜口怯薛官。

translations.literal: His great-grandfather Guiyu served Taizu as official in charge of the keshik of qielian households.
translations.idiomatic: His great-grandfather Guiyu had served Genghis Khan as overseer of the imperial camp's dependent households.

sentences.zh: 祖合剌，袭父职，事世祖。

translations.literal: His grandfather Hela inherited his father's post and served Shizu.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Hela inherited that post and served Kublai.

sentences.zh: 父普兰奚，由宿卫为中书右司员外郎，与丞相哈剌哈孙建议迎立武宗，累迁至山北辽东道肃政廉访使。

translations.literal: His father Pulanxi, from the palace guard, became an outer section vice director of the Right Secretariat of the Central Secretariat; with Chief Councillor Harghasun he proposed welcoming Wuzong to the throne, and through successive promotions reached surveillance commissioner of the Shanbei Liaodong Circuit for rectifying government.
translations.idiomatic: His father Pulanxi rose from the palace guard to an outer-section vice director in the Right Secretariat; with Chief Councillor Harghasun he had urged enthroning Emperor Wuzong and eventually became surveillance commissioner of the Shanbei Liaodong circuit.

sentences.zh: 月鲁帖木兒幼警颖，读书强记，俶傥有大志。

translations.literal: Yuelutiemuer in youth was alert and keen, read books with strong memory, and was bold and unconventional with great ambition.
translations.idiomatic: As a boy Yuelutiemuer was quick-witted and had an exceptional memory; he was bold and high-minded.

sentences.zh: 年十二，成宗命与哈剌哈孙之子脱欢同入国学。

translations.literal: At age twelve, Chengzong ordered him to enter the National University together with Harghasun's son Tuohuan.
translations.idiomatic: At twelve he was ordered by Emperor Chengzong to enter the National University together with Harghasun's son Tuohuan.

sentences.zh: 仁宗时入宿卫，一日，帝顾问左右曰：「斯人容貌不凡，谁之子耶？

translations.literal: Under Renzong he entered the palace guard; one day the emperor asked those beside him: "This man's appearance is out of the ordinary—whose son is he?"
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Renzong he joined the palace guard. One day the emperor asked his attendants, "This young man looks remarkable—whose son is he?"

sentences.zh: 」左右忘其父名，月鲁帖木兒即对曰：「臣父普兰奚也。

translations.literal: " Those beside him forgot his father's name; Yuelutiemuer at once replied: "My father is Pulanxi."
translations.idiomatic: Those around him could not recall the name, but Yuelutiemuer answered at once, "He is my father, Pulanxi."

sentences.zh: 」帝曰：「汝父赞谋以定国难，朕未尝忘。

translations.literal: " The emperor said: "Your father aided with counsel to settle the national crisis; I have never forgotten."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "Your father helped settle the succession crisis with his counsel—I have never forgotten that debt."

sentences.zh: 」因命脱忽台传旨四怯薛扎撒火孙，令常侍禁廷，毋止其入。

translations.literal: " He therefore ordered Tuohutai to convey an edict to the four keshik commanders: let him attend the forbidden court regularly and do not stop his entry.
translations.idiomatic: He then ordered Tuohutai to tell the four keshik commanders that Yuelutiemuer was to attend court freely and must never be turned away.

sentences.zh: 哈剌哈孙欲用为中书蒙古必阇赤，辄辞焉。

translations.literal: Harghasun wished to employ him as a Mongol secretary of the Central Secretariat, but he repeatedly declined.
translations.idiomatic: Harghasun wanted to appoint him a Mongol secretary in the Central Secretariat, but he declined.

sentences.zh: 哈剌哈孙曰：「汝年幼，欲何为乎？

translations.literal: Harghasun said: "You are young—what do you wish to do?"
translations.idiomatic: Harghasun asked, "You are still young—what post do you want?"

sentences.zh: 」对曰：「欲为御史尔。

translations.literal: " He replied: "I wish to be a censor, that is all."
translations.idiomatic: He answered, "I want to be a censor, nothing more."

sentences.zh: 」人壮其志。

translations.literal: " People admired his ambition.
translations.idiomatic: Those who heard it admired his resolve.

sentences.zh: 久之，遂拜监察御史，巡按上都，劾奏太师、右丞相帖木迭兒受张弼赇六万贯，贷死。

translations.literal: After some time he was appointed investigating censor, inspected Shangdu, and impeached the Grand Preceptor and Right Chief Councillor Temuder for accepting sixty thousand strings of cash in bribes from Zhang Bi, commuting a death sentence.
translations.idiomatic: In time he was appointed investigating censor and toured Shangdu, impeaching Grand Preceptor and Right Chief Councillor Temuder for taking sixty thousand strings in bribes from Zhang Bi in exchange for commuting a death sentence.

sentences.zh: 帝怒，碎太师印，赐月鲁帖木兒钞万贯，除兵部郎中，拜殿中侍御史。

translations.literal: The emperor was angry, shattered the Grand Preceptor's seal, bestowed on Yuelutiemuer ten thousand strings of paper money, appointed him a director in the Ministry of War, and invested him as palace attendant censor.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was enraged, broke Temuder's seal of office, rewarded Yuelutiemuer with ten thousand strings of paper money, made him a director in the Ministry of War, and appointed him palace attendant censor.

sentences.zh: 迁给事中、左侍仪、同修起居注。

translations.literal: He was transferred to supervising secretary, left attendant of ceremonies, and co-compiler of the imperial diary.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to supervising secretary, left attendant of ceremonies, and co-compiler of the imperial diary.

sentences.zh: 寻为右司郎中，赐坐便殿，帝顾左右谓曰：「月鲁帖木兒识量明远，可大用者也。

translations.literal: Soon he became a director of the Right Secretariat section; he was granted a seat in the informal hall; the emperor looked to those beside him and said: "Yuelutiemuer's discernment and capacity are clear and far-reaching—he can be greatly employed."
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward he became a director in the Right Secretariat and was granted a seat in the informal audience hall; the emperor told those around him, "Yuelutiemuer is far-sighted and capable—he should be given greater responsibility."

sentences.zh: 」他日，帝语近臣曰：「朕闻前代皆有太上皇之号，今皇太子且长，可居大位，朕欲为太上皇，与若等游观西山以终天年。

translations.literal: " Another day the emperor spoke to close ministers: "I have heard that former ages all had the title Retired Emperor; now the crown prince is already grown and can occupy the great position; I wish to become Retired Emperor and with you roam and view the Western Hills to end my years."
translations.idiomatic: On another day he told his close advisers, "Former dynasties all had retired emperors; our crown prince is grown and can take the throne. I mean to retire as emperor emeritus and spend my last years with you roaming the Western Hills."

sentences.zh: 」御史中丞蛮子、翰林学士明里董阿皆称善。

translations.literal: " Vice censor-in-chief Manzi and Hanlin academician Minglidong'a all praised it as good.
translations.idiomatic: Vice censor-in-chief Manzi and Hanlin academician Minglidong'a both praised the idea.

sentences.zh: 月鲁帖木兒独起拜曰：「臣闻昔之所谓太上皇，若唐玄宗、宋徽宗，皆当祸乱，不得已而为之者也。

translations.literal: Yuelutiemuer alone rose, bowed, and said: "I have heard that the so-called Retired Emperors of old, such as Tang Xuanzong and Song Huizong, all came at times of calamity and disorder and did it because they had no choice."
translations.idiomatic: Yuelutiemuer alone rose and bowed. "The retired emperors of old—Tang Xuanzong, Song Huizong—took that title only amid calamity, when they had no other choice."

sentences.zh: 愿陛下正大位，以保万世无疆之业，前代虚名，何足慕哉！

translations.literal: I wish Your Majesty to hold the great position uprightly, to preserve the enterprise without boundary for ten thousand generations—what is there to admire in empty titles of former ages!
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty should keep the throne in your own hands and secure the realm for generations to come. Why envy a hollow title from troubled times?"

sentences.zh: 」帝善其对。

translations.literal: " The emperor approved his reply.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor approved his answer.

sentences.zh: 仁宗崩，帖木迭兒复入中书，据相位。

translations.literal: Renzong died; Temuder again entered the Central Secretariat and held the chief councillor's position.
translations.idiomatic: When Renzong died, Temuder returned to the Central Secretariat and seized the chief councillor's post.

sentences.zh: 参议乞失监以受人金带系狱，帖木迭兒乃使乞失监诉月鲁帖木兒为御史时诬丞相受赇。

translations.literal: Participating councillor Qishijian was imprisoned for accepting someone's golden belt; Temuder then had Qishijian accuse Yuelutiemuer of, when he was a censor, falsely charging the chief councillor with taking bribes.
translations.idiomatic: Participating councillor Qishijian was jailed for accepting a golden belt as a bribe; Temuder then had him claim that Yuelutiemuer had fabricated bribery charges against him when he was a censor.

sentences.zh: 皇太后命丞相哈散等即徽政院推问不实，事遂释。

translations.literal: The empress dowager ordered Chief Councillor Hasan and others to investigate immediately at the Huizheng Yuan; it was found untrue, and the matter was released.
translations.idiomatic: The empress dowager ordered Chief Councillor Hasan and others to investigate at the Huizheng Yuan; the charge proved false and the case was dropped.

sentences.zh: 帖木迭兒乃奏以月鲁帖木兒为山东盐运司副使，降亚中大夫为承事郎，期月间盐课增以万计。

translations.literal: Temuder then memorialized appointing Yuelutiemuer deputy commissioner of the Shandong Salt Transport Office, demoting him from subordinate grand master of the palace to gentleman for court attendance; within a month salt revenue increased by tens of thousands.
translations.idiomatic: Temuder then had him posted as deputy commissioner of the Shandong Salt Transport Office, demoted from subordinate grand master to gentleman for court attendance; within a month salt revenue rose by tens of thousands of strings.

sentences.zh: 丁外艰，扶丧西还。

translations.literal: He observed mourning for his father and escorted the coffin back west.
translations.idiomatic: When his father died he went into mourning and escorted the coffin westward.

sentences.zh: 擢山南江北道肃政廉访副使。

translations.literal: He was promoted to deputy surveillance commissioner of the Shannan Jiangbei Circuit for rectifying government.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to deputy surveillance commissioner of the Shannan and Jiangbei circuit.

sentences.zh: 泰定初，迁汴梁路总管，再调总管武昌，以养亲不赴。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Taiding he was transferred to prefect of Bianliang Circuit; again he was reassigned as prefect of Wuchang but did not take up the post in order to support his parents.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Taiding reign he was made prefect of Bianliang, then reassigned to Wuchang, but declined both posts to care for his parents.

sentences.zh: 致和元年，河南行省平章伯颜矫制起月鲁帖木兒为本省参知政事，共议起兵。

translations.literal: In the first year of Zhihe, Henan Branch Secretariat Grand Councillor Bayan by forged edict raised Yuelutiemuer as vice administrator of that province to deliberate together on raising troops.
translations.idiomatic: In 1328 Bayan, grand councillor of the Henan Branch Secretariat, forged an edict appointing Yuelutiemuer vice administrator of the province so they could plan a military rising together.

sentences.zh: 月鲁帖木兒固辞曰：「皇子北还，问参政受命何人，则将何辞以对？

translations.literal: Yuelutiemuer firmly declined, saying: "When the prince returns north and asks the vice administrator from whom he received his appointment, what words will there be to answer?"
translations.idiomatic: Yuelutiemuer refused firmly. "When the prince returns from the north and asks under whose authority you made me vice administrator, what answer will you give?"

sentences.zh: 」伯颜怒。

translations.literal: " Bayan was angry.
translations.idiomatic: Bayan was furious.

sentences.zh: 会明里董阿迓皇子过河南，而月鲁帖木兒为御史时尝劾其娶娼女冒受封，明里董阿因说伯颜收之，丞相别不花亦与之有隙，乃谪月鲁帖木兒乾宁安抚司安置。

translations.literal: It happened that Minglidong'a was meeting the prince passing through Henan; when Yuelutiemuer had been a censor he had once impeached him for marrying a prostitute and fraudulently receiving enfeoffment; Minglidong'a therefore urged Bayan to take him in hand; Chief Councillor Biebuhua also had a grudge against him; Yuelutiemuer was therefore demoted and placed under the Qianning Pacification Commission.
translations.idiomatic: Minglidong'a was then escorting the prince through Henan; he reminded Bayan that Yuelutiemuer had once impeached him for marrying a courtesan and fraudulently taking a title. Chief Councillor Biebuhua also bore a grudge, and Yuelutiemuer was banished to serve under the Qianning Pacification Commission.

sentences.zh: 至顺四年，移置雷州。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Zhishun he was moved and placed in Lei Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: In 1333 he was transferred to Lei Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 至元六年，顺帝召之还。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Zhiyuan, Emperor Shundi summoned him back.
translations.idiomatic: In 1340 Emperor Shundi summoned him back to court.

sentences.zh: 至正二年，入觐，帝欲留之，以母丧未葬辞。

translations.literal: In the second year of Zhizheng he came to audience; the emperor wished to keep him, but he declined because his mother's funeral had not yet been buried.
translations.idiomatic: In 1342 he presented himself at court; the emperor wished to keep him in service, but he declined because his mother was not yet buried.

sentences.zh: 四年，乃起同知将作院事。

translations.literal: In the fourth year he was then raised as associate director of the Directorate of Palace Buildings.
translations.idiomatic: In 1344 he was recalled as associate director of the Directorate of Palace Buildings.

sentences.zh: 寻除大宗正府也可札鲁花赤。

translations.literal: Soon he was appointed darughachi of the Grand Imperial Clan Court.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon made darughachi of the Grand Imperial Clan Court.

sentences.zh: 九年，由太医院使拜翰林学士承旨、知经筵事。

translations.literal: In the ninth year, from director of the Imperial Medical Academy he was appointed Hanlin academician-expositor and director of the Classics Mat lectures.
translations.idiomatic: In 1349, after serving as director of the Imperial Medical Academy, he was made expositor-in-chief of the Hanlin Academy and director of the Classics Mat.

sentences.zh: 进读之际，引援经史，一本于王道，帝嘉纳焉。

translations.literal: When lecturing before the throne, he cited the classics and histories, taking the kingly way as his single standard; the emperor praised and accepted it.
translations.idiomatic: In his lectures before the throne he drew on the classics and histories, grounding every point in the principles of benevolent rule, and the emperor warmly approved.

sentences.zh: 十二年，江南诸郡盗贼充斥，诏拜月鲁帖木兒平章政事，行省江浙，因言于丞相脱脱曰：「守御江南，为计已缓，若得从权行事，犹有可为。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year, bandits filled the various prefectures of Jiangnan; he was ordered appointed grand councillor and sent to the Jiang-Zhe Branch Secretariat; he therefore said to Chief Councillor Toghto: "To defend Jiangnan—the plan is already slow; if one may act with discretionary authority, there is still something that can be done."
translations.idiomatic: In 1352, as bandits overran the Jiangnan prefectures, he was appointed grand councillor and sent to the Jiang-Zhe Branch Secretariat. He told Chief Councillor Toghto, "Merely holding Jiangnan on the defensive is already too late; if I may act on discretionary authority, something may still be done."

sentences.zh: 」不从。

translations.literal: " He did not agree.
translations.idiomatic: Toghto refused.

sentences.zh: 陛辞，赐尚醖、御衣、弓矢、甲胄、卫卒十人、钞万五千贯以行。

translations.literal: On taking leave at court he was bestowed imperial wine, imperial robes, bow and arrows, armor, ten guard soldiers, and fifteen thousand strings of paper money for the journey.
translations.idiomatic: On his departure the emperor gave him imperial wine, court robes, bow and arrows, armor, ten guardsmen, and fifteen thousand strings of paper money for the road.

sentences.zh: 比至镇，引僚属集父老询守备之方，招募民兵数千人，号令明肃。

translations.literal: When he reached his post he led his subordinates to gather the elders and fathers and asked about methods of defense, recruited several thousand militiamen, and his orders were clear and strict.
translations.idiomatic: On reaching his command he summoned local elders with his staff to discuss defense, recruited several thousand militiamen, and enforced clear, strict discipline.

sentences.zh: 统师次建德，获首贼何福斩于市，遂复淳安等县，俘获万餘人，复业者三万餘家。

translations.literal: Leading his army he halted at Jiande, captured the chief bandit He Fu and executed him in the market, then recovered Chun'an and other counties, took more than ten thousand captives, and more than thirty thousand households returned to their occupations.
translations.idiomatic: He led his troops to Jiande, captured the rebel leader He Fu and executed him in public, recovered Chun'an and neighboring counties, took more than ten thousand prisoners, and restored more than thirty thousand households to their livelihoods.

sentences.zh: 是年七月，次徽州，以疾卒于军中。

translations.literal: In the seventh month of that year he halted at Huizhou and died of illness in the army.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month of that year he fell ill at Huizhou and died in camp.

sentences.zh: 卜颜铁木兒

translations.literal: Buyantiemuer
translations.idiomatic: Buyantiemuer

sentences.zh: 卜颜铁木兒，字珍卿，唐兀吾密氏。

translations.literal: Buyantiemuer, style name Zhenqing, was of the Tangut Wumi clan.
translations.idiomatic: Buyantiemuer, whose style name was Zhenqing, belonged to the Tangut Wumi clan.

sentences.zh: 性明锐倜傥，早备宿卫，历事武宗、仁宗、英宗。

translations.literal: By nature he was bright, keen, and bold; early he served in the palace guard and attended Wuzong, Renzong, and Yingzong.
translations.idiomatic: Clever, sharp, and bold by nature, he entered the palace guard young and served Emperors Wuzong, Renzong, and Yingzong.

sentences.zh: 天历初，由太常署丞拜监察御史，升殿中侍御史，累除大都路达鲁花赤、都转运盐使、肃政廉访使，由行中书省参知政事升左右丞，擢行御史臺中丞，遂拜江浙行省平章政事。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Tianli, from vice director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices he was appointed investigating censor, promoted to palace attendant censor, and through successive appointments became darughachi of Dadu Circuit, commissioner of salt transport, surveillance commissioner for rectifying government, from vice administrator of the Branch Secretariat to left and right vice administrators, elevated to vice censor-in-chief of the Branch Censorate, and finally appointed grand councillor of the Jiang-Zhe Branch Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Tianli reign he rose from the Court of Imperial Sacrifices to investigating censor and palace attendant censor, then served successively as darughachi of Dadu, salt transport commissioner, and surveillance commissioner before becoming vice administrator, left and right vice administrator, and vice censor-in-chief of the Branch Censorate, and finally grand councillor of the Jiang-Zhe Branch Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 至正十二年春，蕲、黄贼徐寿辉遣兵陷湖广，侵江东、西，诏卜颜铁木兒率军讨之。

translations.literal: In the spring of the twelfth year of Zhizheng, the Qi-Huang bandit Xu Shouhui sent troops that captured Huguang and invaded Jiangdong and Jiangxi; an edict ordered Buyantiemuer to lead an army against them.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of 1352 the rebel Xu Shouhui of Qi and Huang seized Huguang and invaded Jiangdong and Jiangxi; Buyantiemuer was ordered to lead troops against him.

sentences.zh: 卜颜铁木兒益募壮健为兵，得骁勇士三千人、战舰三百艘。

translations.literal: Buyantiemuer further recruited the sturdy and strong as soldiers, obtaining three thousand fierce warriors and three hundred warships.
translations.idiomatic: He raised more troops and assembled three thousand seasoned fighters and three hundred warships.

sentences.zh: 时湖广平章政事也先帖木兒、江西平章政事星吉、江南行台御史中丞蛮子海牙皆以兵驻太平，宿留不进。

translations.literal: At the time Huguang Grand Councillor Yexiantiemuer, Jiangxi Grand Councillor Xingji, and Jiangnan Branch Censorate Vice Censor-in-Chief Manzi Haiya all had troops stationed at Taiping and lingered without advancing.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Councillor Yexiantiemuer of Huguang, Grand Councillor Xingji of Jiangxi, and Vice Censor-in-Chief Manzi Haiya of the Jiangnan Branch Censorate all had armies at Taiping but would not move forward.

sentences.zh: 卜颜帖木兒至，乃与俱前。

translations.literal: When Buyantiemuer arrived, they then advanced together.
translations.idiomatic: When Buyantiemuer arrived, they advanced together.

sentences.zh: 贼方聚丁家洲，官军猝与遇，奋击败之，遂复铜陵县，擒其贼帅，复池州。

translations.literal: The bandits were just gathering at Dingjiazhou; the government army suddenly encountered them, fought fiercely and defeated them, then recovered Tongling County, captured their bandit chief, and recovered Chizhou.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels were massing at Dingjiazhou when government forces met them unexpectedly, routed them, retook Tongling, captured their leader, and recovered Chizhou.

sentences.zh: 遂分遣万户普贤奴屯阳陵，王建中屯白面渡，闾兒讨无为州，而自率镇抚不花、万户明安驻池口，以防遏上流，为之节度。

translations.literal: He then separately sent the ten-thousand-household commander Puxiannu to garrison Yangling, Wang Jianzhong to garrison Baimian Ford, Lv'er to attack Wuwei Prefecture, and himself led the pacification commissioner Buhua and the ten-thousand-household commander Ming'an to garrison Chikou to block the upper reaches, directing operations.
translations.idiomatic: He posted Commander Puxiannu at Yangling, Wang Jianzhong at Baimian Ford, and Lv'er against Wuwei Prefecture, while he himself with Pacification Commissioner Buhua and Commander Ming'an held Chikou to block the upper river and direct operations.

sentences.zh: 已而江州再陷，星吉死之。

translations.literal: Before long Jiang Prefecture fell again and Xingji died there.
translations.idiomatic: Jiang Prefecture soon fell again, and Xingji was killed in the fighting.

sentences.zh: 蛮子海牙及威顺王宽彻普化军俱溃而东。

translations.literal: Manzi Haiya and the army of the Prince of Weishun Kuanchapuhua both collapsed and fled east.
translations.idiomatic: Manzi Haiya and the Prince of Weishun's army both broke and fled eastward.

sentences.zh: 安庆被围益急，遣使来求援。

translations.literal: Anqing was besieged ever more urgently and sent envoys to request aid.
translations.idiomatic: The siege of Anqing tightened, and messengers came begging for relief.

sentences.zh: 诸将皆欲自守信地，卜颜铁木兒曰：「何言之不忠耶！

translations.literal: The generals all wished to hold their own secure territories; Buyantiemuer said: "How disloyal your words are!"
translations.idiomatic: The other generals wanted only to hold their own ground. Buyantiemuer said, "What disloyal talk is this!"

sentences.zh: 安庆与池止隔一水，今安庆固守，是其节也，而救患之义，我其可缓。

translations.literal: Anqing and Chizhou are separated by only one stretch of water; now Anqing holds firm—that is its integrity—but the duty of relieving distress—how can we delay?
translations.idiomatic: Anqing and Chizhou are separated by a single river. Anqing is holding out—that is loyalty—but how can we delay the duty to relieve a neighbor in peril?"

sentences.zh: 且上流官军虽溃，然皆百战之餘，所乏者钱谷器具而已，吾受命总兵，其可视之而不恤哉！

translations.literal: Moreover, though the upper-reach government troops have collapsed, they are all veterans of a hundred battles; what they lack is only money, grain, and equipment; I have received orders to command the army—how can I look on them and not succor them!
translations.idiomatic: The troops upstream may have broken, but they are veterans; they lack only money, grain, and equipment. I command this army—how can I abandon them?"

sentences.zh: 」即大发帑藏以周之，溃军皆大集，而两军之势复振，安庆之围遂解。

translations.literal: " He immediately opened the treasury stores on a large scale to supply them; the collapsed troops all gathered in great numbers, the strength of both armies revived, and the siege of Anqing was thereby lifted.
translations.idiomatic: He opened the treasury and supplied them generously; the scattered troops rallied, both armies regained their strength, and the siege of Anqing was lifted.

sentences.zh: 十三年三月，贼众复来攻池州，众且十万，诸县皆应之。

translations.literal: In the third month of the thirteenth year the bandit masses again came to attack Chizhou; their numbers approached a hundred thousand, and all the counties responded to them.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month of 1353 the rebels attacked Chizhou again with nearly a hundred thousand men, and counties all along the river rose in support.

sentences.zh: 卜颜帖木兒会诸将谋曰：「贼表里连结，若俟其筑垒成而坐食诸县之粟，破之实难。

translations.literal: Buyantiemuer convened the generals and said: "The bandits are linked inside and out; if we wait until they finish building ramparts and live off the grain of the various counties, breaking them will truly be hard."
translations.idiomatic: Buyantiemuer called his generals together and said, "The rebels are linked up and down the river. If we wait until they finish their camps and live off the grain of the surrounding counties, they will be hard to defeat."

sentences.zh: 今新至疲弊，如乘其骄惰，尽锐攻之，则顷刻之间功可成矣。

translations.literal: Now they have newly arrived and are weary and spent; if we seize their arrogance and indolence and attack with all our elite, then in the space of a moment success can be achieved.
translations.idiomatic: They have just arrived and are tired and overconfident. If we strike now with our best troops, we can finish them in a moment."

sentences.zh: 」众曰：「诺。

translations.literal: " The crowd said: "Yes."
translations.idiomatic: They agreed.

sentences.zh: 」遂分番与战，果大败之，擒其伪帅，俘斩无算，诸县复平，遂乘胜率舟师以进。

translations.literal: " They then fought in shifts and indeed inflicted a great defeat, captured their false commander, took and beheaded countless prisoners, the various counties were again pacified, and riding the victory they advanced with the fleet.
translations.idiomatic: They attacked in relays, routed the enemy, captured their commander, and killed countless rebels; the counties were pacified, and they pressed upstream by water.

sentences.zh: 五月，与战于望江，又战小孤山及彭泽，又战龙开河，皆破走之。

translations.literal: In the fifth month they fought at Wangjiang, again at Xiaogushan and Pengze, again at Longkai River, and in each case routed and drove them off.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month they fought at Wangjiang, Xiaogushan, Pengze, and Longkai River, defeating the rebels at every encounter.

sentences.zh: 进复江州，留兵守之。

translations.literal: Advancing, they recovered Jiang Prefecture and left troops to guard it.
translations.idiomatic: They advanced and retook Jiang Prefecture, leaving a garrison behind.

sentences.zh: 七月，进兵攻蕲州，擒其伪帅邹普泰，遂克其城。

translations.literal: In the seventh month they advanced to attack Qi Prefecture, captured the false commander Zou Putai, and then took the city.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month they attacked Qi Prefecture, captured the rebel commander Zou Putai, and took the city.

sentences.zh: 进兵道士洑，焚其栅，抵兰溪口。

translations.literal: Advancing to Daoshifu, they burned their palisades and reached Lanxi Ford.
translations.idiomatic: They pushed on to Daoshifu, burned the rebel stockades, and reached Lanxi Ford.

sentences.zh: 贼之巢曰黄连寨，又克而歼之。

translations.literal: The bandits' nest was called Huanglian Stockade; they again captured it and annihilated them.
translations.idiomatic: They stormed the rebel stronghold at Huanglian Stockade and wiped it out.

sentences.zh: 分兵平两巴河，于是江路始通。

translations.literal: They divided troops to pacify the Two Ba Rivers, and thereby the river route was first opened.
translations.idiomatic: Detachments pacified the Two Ba Rivers, and the Yangzi route was open again.

sentences.zh: 十一月，与蛮子海牙、四川行省参知政事哈临秃、左丞桑秃失里、西宁王牙罕沙军合，而湖广左丞伯颜不花等军皆会。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month he joined with Manzi Haiya, Sichuan Branch Secretariat Vice Administrator Halintu, Left Vice Administrator Sangtuoshili, and the army of the Prince of Xining Yahansha, while the armies of Huguang Left Vice Administrator Bayan Buhua and others all converged.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month his forces joined those of Manzi Haiya, Sichuan Vice Administrator Halintu, Left Vice Administrator Sangtuoshili, the Prince of Xining, and Huguang Vice Administrator Bayan Buhua.

sentences.zh: 十二月，分道进攻蕲水县，拔其伪都，获伪将相而下四百餘人，徐寿辉仅以身免。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month they attacked Qishui County by separate routes, seized their false capital, captured more than four hundred false ministers and generals and below, and Xu Shouhui alone escaped with his body.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month they attacked Qishui County from several directions, took the rebel capital, and captured more than four hundred rebel officials; Xu Shouhui alone escaped.

sentences.zh: 以功诏赐上尊、黄金带。

translations.literal: For merit an edict bestowed superior wine and a golden belt.
translations.idiomatic: For his service the emperor granted him imperial wine and a golden belt.

sentences.zh: 时丞相脱脱方总戎南征，闻诸贼皆已破，乃檄伯颜不花征淮东，蛮子海牙守裕溪口，威顺王还武昌，而卜颜铁木兒独控长江。

translations.literal: At the time Chief Councillor Toghto was just commanding the southern campaign; hearing that all the bandits had been broken, he then issued orders for Bayan Buhua to campaign in Huaidong, Manzi Haiya to guard Yuxi Ford, the Prince of Weishun to return to Wuchang, while Buyantiemuer alone controlled the Yangzi.
translations.idiomatic: Chief Councillor Toghto was then commanding the southern campaign. Learning that the rebels were broken, he ordered Bayan Buhua to Huaidong, Manzi Haiya to hold Yuxi Ford, the Prince of Weishun back to Wuchang, and left Buyantiemuer alone to hold the Yangzi.

sentences.zh: 十六年六月，复以军守池州。

translations.literal: In the sixth month of the sixteenth year he again garrisoned Chizhou with troops.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month of 1356 he again garrisoned Chizhou.

sentences.zh: 十一月，卒。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the eleventh month.

sentences.zh: 卜颜铁木兒持身廉介，人不敢干以私，其为将，所过不受礼遗宴犒，民不知有兵。

translations.literal: Buyantiemuer maintained himself with integrity and austerity; people did not dare approach him with private requests; as a general, wherever he passed he accepted no gifts, banquets, or rewards, and the people were unaware that an army was present.
translations.idiomatic: Buyantiemuer was incorruptible and stern; no one dared solicit him privately. As a commander he accepted no gifts or banquets along the march, and the people scarcely knew an army had passed.

sentences.zh: 性至孝，幼养于叔父阿术，事之如亲父。

translations.literal: By nature he was deeply filial; in youth he was raised by his uncle Ashu and served him as a natural father.
translations.idiomatic: He was deeply filial; raised from childhood by his uncle Ashu, he treated him as his own father.

sentences.zh: 常乘花马，时称为花马兒平章云。

translations.literal: He often rode a piebald horse; at the time he was called the Piebald-Horse Grand Councillor.
translations.idiomatic: He habitually rode a piebald horse and was known as the Piebald-Horse Grand Councillor.

sentences.zh: 星吉，字吉甫，河西人。

translations.literal: Xingji, style name Jifu, was a man of Hexi.
translations.idiomatic: Xingji, whose style name was Jifu, came from Hexi in the northwest.

sentences.zh: 曾祖朵吉，祖搠思吉朵而只，父搠思吉，世事太祖、宪宗、世祖为怯里马赤。

translations.literal: His great-grandfather Duoji, grandfather Suosijiduorezhi, and father Suosiji all served Taizu, Xianzong, and Shizu as imperial attendants.
translations.idiomatic: His great-grandfather Duoji, grandfather Suosijiduorezhi, and father Suosiji had all served Genghis Khan, Möngke, and Kublai as imperial attendants.

sentences.zh: 星吉少给事仁宗潜邸，以精敏称。

translations.literal: Xingji in youth attended Renzong's hidden residence and was known for keen intelligence.
translations.idiomatic: As a youth he served in Renzong's household before the throne and was known for his sharp mind.

sentences.zh: 至治初，授中尚监，改右侍仪，兼修起居注。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Zhizhi he was appointed director of the Central Palace Service, changed to right attendant of ceremonies, and concurrently compiled the imperial diary.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Zhizhi reign he became director of the Central Palace Service, then right attendant of ceremonies and co-compiler of the imperial diary.

sentences.zh: 拜监察御史，有直声。

translations.literal: He was appointed investigating censor and had a reputation for uprightness.
translations.idiomatic: Appointed investigating censor, he earned a reputation for integrity.

sentences.zh: 自是十五迁为宣政院使，出为江南行御史臺御史大夫。

translations.literal: From this he was promoted through fifteen steps to director of the Xuanzheng Yuan and sent out as censor-in-chief of the Jiangnan Branch Censorate.
translations.idiomatic: He rose through fifteen promotions to director of the Xuanzheng Yuan and then censor-in-chief of the Jiangnan Branch Censorate.

sentences.zh: 时承平日久，内外方以观望为政，星吉独持风裁，御史行部，必敕厉而遣之。

translations.literal: At the time peace had lasted long; inside and outside people were just taking a wait-and-see attitude in government; Xingji alone upheld standards of conduct; when censors toured the circuits he always sternly admonished them before sending them off.
translations.idiomatic: After long peace officials everywhere governed by looking the other way; Xingji alone enforced discipline and sternly briefed every censor before dispatch.

sentences.zh: 湖东佥事三宝住，儒者也，性廉介，所至搏贪猾无所贷。

translations.literal: Hudong surveillance vice commissioner Sanbaozhu was a Confucian scholar, by nature upright and austere; wherever he went he struck at the greedy and cunning and spared none.
translations.idiomatic: Sanbaozhu, a Confucian scholar serving as vice commissioner east of the lake, was incorruptible and relentless against the greedy wherever he went.

sentences.zh: 御史有以自私请者，拒不纳，则诬以事劾之。

translations.literal: A censor made a private request to him; he refused to accept it, so the censor falsely charged him with a matter and impeached him.
translations.idiomatic: When a censor tried to solicit a private favor, he refused; the censor then fabricated charges and impeached him.

sentences.zh: 章至，星吉怒曰：「若人之廉，孰不知之，乃敢为是言耶！

translations.literal: When the memorial arrived, Xingji angrily said: "This man's integrity—who does not know it? Yet you dare speak such words!"
translations.idiomatic: When the memorial arrived, Xingji exclaimed in anger, "Everyone knows this man's integrity—how dare you make such an accusation!"

sentences.zh: 」即奏杖御史而白其诬。

translations.literal: " He immediately memorialized to cane the censor and declare the false charge.
translations.idiomatic: He had the censor beaten and cleared Sanbaozhu of the false charge.

sentences.zh: 执政者恶之，移湖广行省平章政事。

translations.literal: Those in power hated him and transferred him to grand councillor of the Huguang Branch Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: The ministers at court disliked him and transferred him to grand councillor of the Huguang Branch Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 湖广地连江北，威顺王岁尝出猎，民病之。

translations.literal: Huguang's territory connected with the north of the river; the Prince of Weishun every year went out hunting, and the people suffered from it.
translations.idiomatic: Huguang bordered the Yangzi north bank, and every year the Prince of Weishun's hunting parties tormented the people.

sentences.zh: 又起广乐园，多萃名倡巨贾以网大利，有司莫敢忤。

translations.literal: He also raised the Broad Joy Garden, gathering many famous entertainers and great merchants to net great profit; the officials did not dare oppose him.
translations.idiomatic: He also built the Broad Joy Garden, gathering famous entertainers and wealthy merchants to reap huge profits, and no local official dared oppose him.

sentences.zh: 星吉至，谒王，王阖中门，启左扉，召以入。

translations.literal: When Xingji arrived he called on the prince; the prince closed the central gate and opened the left side door to summon him in.
translations.idiomatic: On arriving, Xingji called on the prince, who shut the main gate and admitted him only through the side door.

sentences.zh: 星吉引绳床坐王中门西，言曰：「吾受天子命来作牧，非王私臣也，焉得由不正之道入乎！

translations.literal: Xingji drew a rope bed and sat west of the prince's central gate, saying: "I have received the Son of Heaven's command to come as governor; I am not the prince's private servant—how can I enter by an improper way!"
translations.idiomatic: Xingji set out a rope bed and sat west of the central gate, saying, "I come as the emperor's governor, not as your private retainer—how can I enter by a side door?"

sentences.zh: 」阍者惧，入告王，王命启中门。

translations.literal: " The gatekeeper was afraid, went in to tell the prince, and the prince ordered the central gate opened.
translations.idiomatic: The gatekeeper fled inside in alarm; the prince ordered the main gate opened.

sentences.zh: 星吉入，责王曰：「王帝室之懿，古之所谓伯父叔父者也。

translations.literal: Xingji entered and reproached the prince: "Your Highness is of the imperial clan's excellence—what the ancients called paternal uncle or maternal uncle."
translations.idiomatic: Xingji entered and rebuked him: "Your Highness is of the imperial house—the sort of prince the ancients called royal uncle."

sentences.zh: 今德音不闻，而骋猎宣淫，贾怨于下，恐非所以自贻多福也。

translations.literal: Now your virtuous reputation is not heard, yet you gallop to hunt and display dissipation, buying resentment below—I fear this is not the way to bestow much blessing on yourself.
translations.idiomatic: Yet no word of your virtue reaches the people, while you hunt and indulge yourself and breed resentment below—I fear that is no way to secure your own blessing."

sentences.zh: 」王急握星吉手谢之，为悉罢其所为。

translations.literal: " The prince hastily grasped Xingji's hand and apologized, and on his account completely stopped what he had been doing.
translations.idiomatic: The prince seized his hand in apology and abandoned all these practices.

sentences.zh: 有胡僧曰小住持者，服三品命，恃宠横甚，数以事凌轹官府。

translations.literal: There was a Hu monk called the Little Abbot who wore third-rank orders, relied on favor and was extremely overbearing, and repeatedly on various matters bullied the government offices.
translations.idiomatic: A Central Asian monk known as the Little Abbot held third-rank rank, abused imperial favor, and repeatedly browbeat local officials.

sentences.zh: 星吉命掩捕之，得妻妾女乐妇女十有八人，狱具，罪而籍之，由是豪强敛手，贫弱称快。

translations.literal: Xingji ordered a secret arrest; they obtained eighteen wives, concubines, female musicians, and women; the case was complete, he was convicted and his property registered; thereby the powerful drew back their hands and the poor and weak rejoiced.
translations.idiomatic: Xingji had him seized in secret and found eighteen wives, concubines, and female musicians; the case was complete, he was convicted and his property confiscated, and the powerful shrank back while the poor rejoiced.

sentences.zh: 至正十一年，汝、颍妖贼起，会僚属议之，或曰：「有郑万户，老将也，宜起而用之。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year of Zhizheng, demonic bandits rose in Ru and Ying; he convened his subordinates to discuss it; some said: "There is Commander Zheng, an old general—it is fitting to raise and employ him."
translations.idiomatic: In 1351 rebels rose in Ru and Ying. At a council of his staff someone said, "Commander Zheng is an old general—we should recall him."

sentences.zh: 」星吉乃命募士兵，完城池，修器械，严巡警，悉以其事属郑。

translations.literal: " Xingji then ordered recruitment of militia soldiers, completion of city walls, repair of weapons, strict patrols, and entrusted all these matters to Zheng.
translations.idiomatic: Xingji ordered militia raised, walls repaired, weapons readied, and patrols tightened, placing everything under Zheng's command.

sentences.zh: 贼闻之，遣其党二千来约降。

translations.literal: The bandits heard of it and sent two thousand of their party to arrange a surrender.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels heard of these preparations and sent two thousand men offering to surrender.

sentences.zh: 星吉与郑谋曰：「此诈也，然降而却之，于是为不宜，宜受而审之可也。

translations.literal: Xingji and Zheng plotted, saying: "This is a deception; yet if they surrender and we reject them, that would be improper—it is fitting to accept them and investigate."
translations.idiomatic: Xingji and Zheng agreed: "This is a ruse, but if we refuse them after they offer surrender we will look weak—we should accept them and investigate."

sentences.zh: 」果得其情，乃歼之，械其渠魁数十人以俟命。

translations.literal: " They indeed got the facts, then annihilated them, put shackles on several tens of their ringleaders and awaited orders.
translations.idiomatic: Their plot was exposed; he destroyed them and shackled dozens of leaders pending orders from court.

sentences.zh: 适有旨召为大司农。

translations.literal: Just then an edict summoned him as minister of agriculture.
translations.idiomatic: Just then an edict summoned him to court as minister of agriculture.

sentences.zh: 同僚受贼赂，且嫉其功，乃诬郑罪，释其所械者。

translations.literal: A colleague accepted bandit bribes and, jealous of his achievement, falsely charged Zheng with a crime and released those he had shackled.
translations.idiomatic: A colleague who had taken rebel bribes and envied Xingji's success fabricated charges against Zheng and released the prisoners.

sentences.zh: 明日，贼大至，内外响应，城遂陷。

translations.literal: The next day the bandits came in great force, inside and outside responded, and the city fell.
translations.idiomatic: The next day the rebels came in force, the city rose inside and out, and Wuchang fell.

sentences.zh: 武昌之人骈首夜泣曰：「大夫不去，吾岂为俘囚乎？

translations.literal: The people of Wuchang, heads together, wept by night, saying: "Had the great officer not left, how could we have become captives?"
translations.idiomatic: The people of Wuchang wept together at night: "If our governor had not left, how could we have become captives?"

sentences.zh: 」星吉既入见，具陈贼本末。

translations.literal: " After Xingji entered for audience he fully stated the bandits' origin and end.
translations.idiomatic: At court Xingji reported the whole course of the rebellion.

sentences.zh: 帝大喜，命赐食。

translations.literal: The emperor was greatly pleased and ordered food bestowed.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was delighted and ordered a meal served to him.

sentences.zh: 时宰不悦，奏为江西行省平章政事，员外置。

translations.literal: The chief ministers were displeased and memorialized appointing him grand councillor of the Jiangxi Branch Secretariat, established outside the regular quota.
translations.idiomatic: The chief ministers were displeased and had him posted as grand councillor of Jiangxi on an extraordinary appointment.

sentences.zh: 星吉至江东，诏令守江州。

translations.literal: When Xingji reached Jiangdong, an edict ordered him to guard Jiang Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: When he reached the lower Yangzi, an edict ordered him to hold Jiang Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 时江州已陷，贼据池阳。

translations.literal: At the time Jiang Prefecture had already fallen and the bandits held Chiyang.
translations.idiomatic: Jiang Prefecture had already fallen, and the rebels held Chiyang.

sentences.zh: 太平官军止有三百人，贼号百万，众皆欲走。

translations.literal: The Taiping government troops numbered only three hundred; the bandits claimed a million; the crowd all wished to flee.
translations.idiomatic: At Taiping he had only three hundred government troops while the rebels claimed a million men, and everyone wanted to flee.

sentences.zh: 星吉曰：「畏贼而逃，非勇也；

translations.literal: Xingji said: "To fear bandits and flee is not courage;"
translations.idiomatic: Xingji said, "To flee from fear of the enemy is not courage;"

sentences.zh: 坐而待攻，非智也。

translations.literal: to sit and await attack is not wisdom.
translations.idiomatic: to sit and wait to be attacked is not wisdom.

sentences.zh: 汝等皆有妻子财物，纵逃其可免乎？

translations.literal: You all have wives, children, and property—even if you flee, can you escape?
translations.idiomatic: You all have wives, children, and property—do you think flight will save you?"

sentences.zh: 」乃贷富人钱，募人为兵。

translations.literal: " He then borrowed money from the wealthy and recruited men as soldiers.
translations.idiomatic: He borrowed from the wealthy and recruited troops.

sentences.zh: 先是，行台募兵，人给百五十千，无应者。

translations.literal: Previously the Branch Censorate recruited soldiers, giving each person one hundred fifty thousand cash, and no one responded.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier the Branch Censorate had offered one hundred fifty thousand cash per recruit and found no takers.

sentences.zh: 至是，星吉募兵，人五十千，从争赴之，一日得三千人。

translations.literal: At this time Xingji recruited soldiers, fifty thousand cash per person; followers vied to go; in one day he obtained three thousand men.
translations.idiomatic: Xingji now offered fifty thousand per man, and recruits flocked in; in a single day he raised three thousand troops.

sentences.zh: 乃具舟楫直趋铜陵，克之。

translations.literal: He then prepared boats and ships and went straight to Tongling and captured it.
translations.idiomatic: He fitted out a fleet, struck straight for Tongling, and took it.

sentences.zh: 又破贼白马湾。

translations.literal: He again defeated the bandits at Baima Bay.
translations.idiomatic: He defeated the rebels again at Baima Bay.

sentences.zh: 贼败走，分兵蹑之，抵白湄。

translations.literal: The bandits were defeated and fled; he divided troops to pursue them and reached Baimai.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels fled; he sent detachments in pursuit as far as Baimai.

sentences.zh: 贼穷急，回拒官军，官军乘胜奋击，贼尽殪，擒其渠魁周驴，夺船六百艘，军声大振，遂复池州。

translations.literal: The bandits in desperate straits turned back to resist the government army; the government army, riding the victory, fought fiercely; the bandits were all destroyed, their ringleader Zhou Lü was captured, six hundred ships were seized, military prestige greatly rose, and Chizhou was then recovered.
translations.idiomatic: Cornered, the rebels turned to fight; government forces pressed the attack and annihilated them, capturing their leader Zhou Lü and six hundred boats. Morale soared, and Chizhou was recovered.

sentences.zh: 乃命诸将分道讨贼，复石埭诸县。

translations.literal: He then ordered the generals to attack the bandits by separate routes and recovered Shizhi and other counties.
translations.idiomatic: He sent his generals in several columns against the rebels and recovered Shizhi and neighboring counties.

sentences.zh: 贼复来攻，命王惟恭列阵当之，锋始交，出小舰从旁横击，大破走之，进据清水湾。

translations.literal: The bandits again came to attack; he ordered Wang Weigong to form battle lines to meet them; as the fronts had just engaged, he sent out small ships to strike from the side crosswise, inflicted a great defeat and drove them off, and advanced to occupy Qingshui Bay.
translations.idiomatic: When the rebels attacked again he had Wang Weigong form the line; as battle was joined he sent light craft to strike from the flank, routed them, and advanced to Qingshui Bay.

sentences.zh: 伺者告贼舰至自上流，顺风举帆，众且数十倍，诸将失色。

translations.literal: Scouts reported that bandit ships were coming from upstream, raising sails with the wind; their numbers were nearly ten times greater; the generals turned pale.
translations.idiomatic: Scouts reported rebel ships coming downstream under full sail, nearly ten times their strength; the generals turned pale.

sentences.zh: 星吉曰：「无伤也，风势盛，彼仓卒必不得泊，但伏横港中偃旗以待，俟过而击之，无不胜矣。

translations.literal: Xingji said: "No harm; the wind is strong—they in haste surely cannot moor; only hide in the cross-channel with flags lowered and wait; when they pass then strike them—there is none not victorious."
translations.idiomatic: Xingji said, "Do not worry. With this wind they cannot stop in time. Hide in the side channel with flags down and strike as they pass—we cannot fail."

sentences.zh: 」风怒水驶，贼奄忽而过，乃命举旗张帆鼓噪而薄之，官军殊死战，风反为我用，又大破之。

translations.literal: " The wind was furious and the water swift; the bandits suddenly passed by; he then ordered flags raised, sails spread, drums and shouts, and closed on them; the government army fought to the death; the wind turned to serve them, and they again inflicted a great defeat.
translations.idiomatic: The wind drove the rebel fleet past before they could anchor; he raised flags, set sail, and closed in with drums and shouts. His men fought desperately, the wind shifted in their favor, and they won another great victory.

sentences.zh: 时贼久围安庆，捷闻，遽烧营走。

translations.literal: At the time the bandits had long besieged Anqing; when news of the victory arrived, they hastily burned their camps and fled.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels had long besieged Anqing; when news of his victory arrived, they burned their camps and fled.

sentences.zh: 进复湖口县，克江州，留兵守之。

translations.literal: Advancing, he recovered Hukou County, captured Jiang Prefecture, and left troops to guard it.
translations.idiomatic: He advanced, retook Hukou County, captured Jiang Prefecture, and left a garrison.

sentences.zh: 命王惟恭栅小孤山，而星吉自据番阳口，缀江湖要冲以图恢复。

translations.literal: He ordered Wang Weigong to fortify Xiaogushan, while Xingji himself held Poyang Ford, linking the vital points of the rivers and lakes to plan recovery.
translations.idiomatic: He posted Wang Weigong at Xiaogushan while he himself held Poyang Ford, blocking the key river junctions in hope of restoring the region.

sentences.zh: 时湖广已陷，江西被围，淮、浙亦多故，卒无继援之者，日久粮益乏，士卒咸困。

translations.literal: At the time Huguang had already fallen, Jiangxi was besieged, Huai and Zhe also had many troubles, and in the end there was no one to bring continuing aid; as days lengthened grain grew ever scarcer and the soldiers were all distressed.
translations.idiomatic: Huguang had fallen, Jiangxi was encircled, and Huai and Zhe were in turmoil as well; no reinforcements came, supplies dwindled, and his troops were exhausted.

sentences.zh: 或曰：「东南完实，盍因粮以图再举乎？

translations.literal: Some said: "The southeast is intact and solid—why not rely on its grain to plan another effort?"
translations.idiomatic: Someone suggested, "The southeast is still intact—why not withdraw there on its grain and try again?"

sentences.zh: 」星吉曰：「吾受命守江西，必死于此。

translations.literal: " Xingji said: "I received orders to guard Jiangxi—I must die here."
translations.idiomatic: Xingji replied, "I was ordered to hold Jiangxi, and I will die here."

sentences.zh: 」众莫敢复言。

translations.literal: " The crowd did not dare speak again.
translations.idiomatic: No one dared argue further.

sentences.zh: 有顷，贼乘大船四集，来攻我军，取蒹苇编为大筏，塞上下流火之。

translations.literal: Before long the bandits, riding large ships gathered from four sides, came to attack our army; they took reeds and rushes woven into great rafts, blocked the upper and lower reaches, and set them afire.
translations.idiomatic: Soon rebel great ships closed in from every side. They wove reeds into huge rafts, blocked the river above and below, and set them ablaze.

sentences.zh: 我军力战，众死且尽。

translations.literal: Our army fought fiercely; the host died and was exhausted.
translations.idiomatic: Government forces fought to the last man until nearly all were dead.

sentences.zh: 星吉之从子伯不华与亲兵数十人死之。

translations.literal: Xingji's nephew son Bobuhua and several tens of personal troops died there.
translations.idiomatic: Xingji's nephew Bobuhua and several dozen of his personal guard died with him.

sentences.zh: 星吉犹坚坐不动。

translations.literal: Xingji still sat firmly without moving.
translations.idiomatic: Xingji still sat unmoved.

sentences.zh: 贼发矢射星吉，乃昏仆。

translations.literal: The bandits shot arrows at Xingji, and he then fainted and fell.
translations.idiomatic: Rebel arrows struck him down in a faint.

sentences.zh: 贼素闻星吉名，不忍害，舁置密室中，至旦乃苏。

translations.literal: The bandits had long heard Xingji's name and could not bear to harm him; they carried him and placed him in a secret room; by dawn he revived.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels had long respected his name and would not kill him; they carried him to a hidden room, and he revived at dawn.

sentences.zh: 贼罗拜，争馈以食。

translations.literal: The bandits bowed in a circle and vied to present food.
translations.idiomatic: They bowed around him and competed to bring him food.

sentences.zh: 星吉斥之，遂不复食。

translations.literal: Xingji rebuked them and thereafter ate no more.
translations.idiomatic: He rebuked them and refused to eat again.

sentences.zh: 凡七日，乃自力而起，北面再拜曰：「臣力竭矣。

translations.literal: For seven days in all, he then by his own strength rose, bowed twice facing north, and said: "Your servant's strength is exhausted."
translations.idiomatic: After seven days he forced himself up, bowed twice toward the north, and said, "I have done all I can for Your Majesty."

sentences.zh: 」遂绝，年五十七。

translations.literal: " He then expired; he was fifty-seven.
translations.idiomatic: Then he died, at the age of fifty-seven.

sentences.zh: 星吉为人公廉明决，及在军中，能与将士同甘苦，以忠义感激人心，故能以少击众、得人死力云。

translations.literal: Xingji as a man was fair, incorruptible, clear, and decisive; when in the army he could share hardship and ease with officers and soldiers, and with loyalty and righteousness moved people's hearts; therefore he could strike the many with the few and obtain men's death-defying effort.
translations.idiomatic: Xingji was upright, incorruptible, and resolute; in camp he shared hardship with his men and inspired them with loyalty, and so with few troops he could defeat many and win their utmost devotion.

sentences.zh: 福寿，唐兀人。

translations.literal: Fushou was a Tangut.
translations.idiomatic: Fushou was a Tangut.

sentences.zh: 幼俊茂，知读书，尤善应对。

translations.literal: In youth he was handsome and flourishing, knew how to read books, and was especially skilled in repartee.
translations.idiomatic: As a boy he was handsome and bright, well read, and especially quick in conversation.

sentences.zh: 既长，入备环卫，用年劳授长宁寺少卿，改引进使，升知侍仪使，进正使。

translations.literal: When grown he entered service in the palace guard; for years of service he was appointed vice director of the Changning Temple, changed to introduction commissioner, promoted to director of the Ceremonies Office, and advanced to chief commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: When grown he joined the palace guard, then rose through the Changning Temple and the introduction and ceremonies offices to chief commissioner of court ritual.

sentences.zh: 出为饶州路达鲁花赤，擢淮西廉访副使。

translations.literal: Sent out as darughachi of Raozhou Circuit, he was promoted to deputy surveillance commissioner of Huaixi.
translations.idiomatic: He was posted as darughachi of Raozhou, then promoted to deputy surveillance commissioner of western Huai.

sentences.zh: 入为工部侍郎，佥太常礼仪院事，拜监察御史，改户部侍郎，升尚书，出为燕南廉访使，又五迁为同知枢密院事。

translations.literal: He entered as vice minister of works, concurrent commissioner of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, appointed investigating censor, changed to vice minister of revenue, promoted to minister, sent out as surveillance commissioner of Yannan, and through five more promotions became vice director of the Bureau of Military Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He returned to court as vice minister of works and commissioner of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, served as investigating censor and vice minister then minister of revenue, was surveillance commissioner of Yannan, and after five more promotions became vice director of the Bureau of Military Affairs.

sentences.zh: 至正十一年，颍州以贼反告，时车驾在上都，朝堂皆犹豫未决，欲驿奏以待命。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year of Zhizheng, Ying Prefecture reported rebellion by bandits; at the time the imperial carriage was at Shangdu; the court all hesitated and had not decided, wishing to report by post relay and await orders.
translations.idiomatic: In 1351 Ying Prefecture reported a rebel rising; the emperor was at Shangdu, and the court hesitated, planning to report by courier and wait for orders.

sentences.zh: 福寿独以谓「比使得请还，则事有弗及矣」。

translations.literal: Fushou alone held that "by the time the envoy obtains permission and returns, matters will not be in time."
translations.idiomatic: Fushou alone said, "By the time a messenger returns with permission, it will be too late."

sentences.zh: 于是决议调兵五百，遣卫官哈剌章、忻都、怯来讨之而后以闻。

translations.literal: Thereupon they resolved to transfer five hundred troops and send guard officers Halazhang, Xindu, and Qie to suppress them and afterward report.
translations.idiomatic: They decided to dispatch five hundred troops under guard officers Halazhang, Xindu, and Qie to suppress the rebels and report afterward.

sentences.zh: 顺帝善其处事得宜，明年，改也可札鲁忽赤。

translations.literal: Emperor Shundi approved his handling matters as fitting; the next year he was changed to yeke jarquchi.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Shundi praised his judgment; the following year he was made a yeke jarquchi.

sentences.zh: 未几，出为淮南行省平章政事。

translations.literal: Before long he was sent out as grand councillor of the Huainan Branch Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Shortly afterward he was posted as grand councillor of the Huainan Branch Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 是时濠、泗俱已陷，师久无功。

translations.literal: At the time Hao and Si had both fallen; the army for long had no achievement.
translations.idiomatic: Hao and Si had both fallen, and the campaign had stalled without success.

sentences.zh: 福寿至，督战甚急，而上游贼势甚汹涌，福寿乃议筑石头，断江面，守御有方，众恃以为固。

translations.literal: When Fushou arrived he pressed battle very urgently; upstream the bandit force was very surging; Fushou then proposed building Shitou, cutting off the river surface, with defense in good order; the host relied on it as secure.
translations.idiomatic: Fushou pressed the fighting hard; upstream the rebels were overwhelming. He proposed fortifying Shitou to block the Yangzi, organized the defense well, and the troops took heart.

sentences.zh: 十五年，迁江南行台御史大夫。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year he was transferred to censor-in-chief of the Jiangnan Branch Censorate.
translations.idiomatic: In 1355 he was made censor-in-chief of the Jiangnan Branch Censorate.

sentences.zh: 先是，集庆尝有警，阿鲁灰以湖广平章政事将苗军来援，事平，其军镇扬州。

translations.literal: Previously Jiqing had once had an alarm; Aruhui as Huguang grand councillor led Miao troops to aid; when the matter was settled, his army garrisoned Yangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, when Jiqing was threatened, Aruhui had led Miao troops from Huguang to its relief; after the crisis his army remained at Yangzhou.

sentences.zh: 而阿鲁灰御军无纪律，苗蛮素犷悍，日事杀虏，莫能治。

translations.literal: But Aruhui commanded the army without discipline; the Miao barbarians were by nature fierce and bold, daily engaged in killing and plunder, and no one could control them.
translations.idiomatic: Aruhui could not discipline them; the Miao were naturally fierce and plundered daily, and no one could restrain them.

sentences.zh: 俄而苗军杀阿鲁灰以叛，而集庆之援遂绝。

translations.literal: Before long the Miao army killed Aruhui in rebellion, and Jiqing's aid was thereby cut off.
translations.idiomatic: Soon the Miao troops killed Aruhui in mutiny, and Jiqing lost its last outside support.

sentences.zh: 及高邮、庐、和等州相继沦陷，而集庆势益孤，人心益震恐，且仓库无积蓄，计未知所出，于是民乃愿为兵以自守。

translations.literal: When Gaoyou, Lu, He, and other prefectures successively fell, Jiqing's position grew ever more isolated, people's hearts grew ever more shaken with fear, and moreover the storehouses had no reserves; plans were not known where to go—thereupon the people wished to become soldiers to defend themselves.
translations.idiomatic: As Gaoyou, Lu, He, and other prefectures fell in turn, Jiqing grew more isolated, panic spread, and the granaries were empty. With no plan in sight, the people volunteered to take up arms in self-defense.

sentences.zh: 福寿因下令民多赀者皆助以粮饷，激厉士众，为完守计。

translations.literal: Fushou thereupon ordered that wealthy civilians all assist with grain and provisions, roused the soldiers and populace, and made plans for complete defense.
translations.idiomatic: Fushou ordered wealthy households to contribute grain and supplies, roused the troops, and organized a full defense of the city.

sentences.zh: 朝廷知其劳，数赏赉焉。

translations.literal: The court knew his labor and repeatedly rewarded him.
translations.idiomatic: The court recognized his efforts and rewarded him repeatedly.

sentences.zh: 十六年三月，大明兵围集庆，福寿数督兵出战，尽闭诸城门，独开东门以通出入，而城中势不复能支，城遂破。

translations.literal: In the third month of the sixteenth year, Great Ming troops besieged Jiqing; Fushou repeatedly urged the army to sally and fight; he closed all the city gates and opened only the east gate for passage in and out; but the situation in the city could no longer be sustained, and the city fell.
