translations.idiomatic: In the third month of 1356 Ming forces besieged Jiqing. Fushou led repeated sorties, closed every gate but the east for supply, but the city could not hold and fell.

sentences.zh: 百司皆奔溃，福寿乃独据胡床坐凤凰台下，指麾左右。

translations.literal: All the offices fled and collapsed; Fushou alone occupied a folding chair and sat beneath the Phoenix Terrace, directing those left and right.
translations.idiomatic: Every office fled in chaos; Fushou alone sat on a camp chair beneath the Phoenix Terrace, still giving orders to his attendants.

sentences.zh: 或劝之去，叱之曰：「吾为国家重臣，城存则生，城破则死，尚安往哉！

translations.literal: Some urged him to leave; he rebuked them, saying: "I am a great minister of the state—if the city stands I live, if the city falls I die—where else would I go!"
translations.idiomatic: When someone urged him to flee, he snapped, "I am a great minister of the dynasty. If the city stands I live; if it falls I die. Where would I go?"

sentences.zh: 」达鲁花赤达尼达思见其独坐若有所为者，从问所决，留弗去。

translations.literal: " The darughachi Danis, seeing him sit alone as if about to do something, followed and asked his decision, and stayed without leaving.
translations.idiomatic: The darughachi Danis saw him sitting alone as if resolved on something, asked his intention, and stayed at his side.

sentences.zh: 俄而乱兵四集，福寿遂遇害，不知所在，达尼达思亦死之。

translations.literal: Before long disorderly troops gathered from four sides; Fushou was then killed, his whereabouts unknown; Danis also died there.
translations.idiomatic: Rebel troops soon closed in from every side; Fushou was killed, his body never found, and Danis died with him.

sentences.zh: 又同时死者，有治书侍御史贺方。

translations.literal: Also dying at the same time was drafting secretary attendant censor He Fang.
translations.idiomatic: Drafting secretary attendant censor He Fang died at the same time.

sentences.zh: 达尼达思字思明。

translations.literal: Danis's style name was Siming.
translations.idiomatic: Danis's style name was Siming.

sentences.zh: 贺方字伯京，晋宁人，以文学名。

translations.literal: He Fang's style name was Bojing; he was a man of Jinning, famous for literary learning.
translations.idiomatic: He Fang, style name Bojing, was from Jinning and famed for his literary accomplishments.

sentences.zh: 事闻，朝廷赠福寿金紫光禄大夫、江浙行省左丞相、上柱国，追封卫国公，谥忠肃。

translations.literal: When the matter was reported, the court posthumously bestowed on Fushou the title Golden Purple Light Grand Master, left chief councillor of the Jiang-Zhe Branch Secretariat, and supreme pillar of state, enfeoffed him posthumously as Duke of Weiguo, with posthumous title Zhongsu.
translations.idiomatic: When word reached court, Fushou was posthumously made Golden Purple Light Grand Master, left chief councillor of the Jiang-Zhe Branch Secretariat, and supreme pillar of state, enfeoffed as Duke of Wei with the posthumous title Loyal and Stern.

sentences.zh: 道童，高昌人，自号石岩。

translations.literal: Daotong was a man of Gaochang and styled himself Shiyan.
translations.idiomatic: Daotong was a native of Gaochang who took the sobriquet Stone Cliff.

sentences.zh: 性深沉寡言。

translations.literal: By nature he was deep and reserved and spoke little.
translations.idiomatic: He was deep and reserved and spoke little.

sentences.zh: 以世胄入官，授直省舍人，历官清显，素负能名。

translations.literal: Through hereditary status he entered office, was appointed a direct-secretariat attendant, passed through clear and eminent posts, and long bore a reputation for ability.
translations.idiomatic: He entered office by hereditary privilege as a direct-secretariat attendant, rose through prominent posts, and was long known for his competence.

sentences.zh: 调信州路总管，移平江，皆以善政称。

translations.literal: Transferred as prefect of Xinzhou Circuit and moved to Pingjiang—both were praised for good government.
translations.idiomatic: As prefect of Xinzhou and then of Pingjiang he won praise for good government.

sentences.zh: 至正元年，迁大都路达鲁花赤，出为江浙行省参知政事，寻召参政中书，顷之，又出为江浙行省右丞，遂升本省平章政事。

translations.literal: In the first year of Zhizheng he was transferred to darughachi of Dadu Circuit, sent out as vice administrator of the Jiang-Zhe Branch Secretariat, soon summoned as participating administrator of the Central Secretariat, shortly afterward again sent out as right vice administrator of the Jiang-Zhe Branch Secretariat, and then promoted to grand councillor of that province.
translations.idiomatic: In 1341 he became darughachi of Dadu, then vice administrator of the Jiang-Zhe Branch Secretariat, was recalled to the Central Secretariat, returned as right vice administrator of Jiang-Zhe, and was promoted to grand councillor of the province.

sentences.zh: 十一年，诏仍以平章政事行省江西。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year an edict again appointed him grand councillor administering Jiangxi.
translations.idiomatic: In 1351 an edict sent him back to Jiangxi as grand councillor.

sentences.zh: 是年，贼起蕲、黄，平章政事秃坚理不花将兵捍江州。

translations.literal: That year bandits rose in Qi and Huang; Grand Councillor Tujianlibuhua led troops to defend Jiang Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: That year rebels rose in Qi and Huang; Grand Councillor Tujianlibuhua led troops to hold Jiang Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 既而土寇蜂起，道童素不知兵事，仓皇无所措。

translations.literal: Before long local bandits swarmed forth; Daotong had never known military affairs and in panic had nowhere to turn.
translations.idiomatic: Local bandits soon swarmed up everywhere; Daotong knew nothing of military affairs and was at a loss.

sentences.zh: 左右司郎中普颜不花曰：「今贼势冲突，城中无备，万一失守，奈何？

translations.literal: Left and Right Secretariat section director Puyanbuhua said: "Now the bandit force clashes violently; the city has no preparations—if by chance we lose it, what then?"
translations.idiomatic: Left and Right Secretariat director Puyanbuhua said, "The rebels are pressing hard and the city is unprepared. If it falls, what then?"

sentences.zh: 有章伯颜左丞者，致仕居抚州，其人熟知军务，宜以便宜礼请之，使署本省左丞事，专任调遣军旅，庶幾事有可济。

translations.literal: There is former Left Vice Administrator Zhang Boyan, retired and living in Fuzhou—this man is well versed in military affairs; it is fitting to invite him with discretionary courtesy, have him act in the province's left vice administrator affairs, and specially charge him with dispatching the army—perhaps matters can be helped.
translations.idiomatic: Former Left Vice Administrator Zhang Boyan lives in retirement at Fuzhou and knows military affairs well. We should invite him with full courtesy, let him act as left vice administrator, and put the army under his command—then something may yet be done."

sentences.zh: 」道童从其言，而伯颜亦欣然为起，曰：「此正我报国之秋也。

translations.literal: " Daotong followed his words; Boyan also gladly rose for the task, saying: "This is just the season for me to repay the state."
translations.idiomatic: Daotong agreed, and Zhang Boyan gladly came out of retirement, saying, "This is my time to serve the dynasty."

sentences.zh: 」至则与普颜不花设御敌计甚悉。

translations.literal: " When he arrived he and Puyanbuhua laid plans against the enemy in great detail.
translations.idiomatic: On arrival he and Puyanbuhua worked out a detailed plan of defense.

sentences.zh: 明年正月，湖广陷，秃坚里不花由江州遁还。

translations.literal: In the first month of the next year Huguang fell; Tujianlibuhua fled back from Jiang Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the following year Huguang fell, and Tujianlibuhua fled back from Jiang Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 二月，普颜不花将兵往江州，至石头渡，遇贼战败，道童闻之大恐，即怀省印遁走。

translations.literal: In the second month Puyanbuhua led troops toward Jiang Prefecture; at Shitou Ford he met the bandits and was defeated; Daotong heard and was greatly afraid, immediately took the provincial seal and fled.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month Puyanbuhua marched on Jiang Prefecture, was defeated at Shitou Ford, and Daotong, terrified, fled with the provincial seal.

sentences.zh: 普颜不花还，与伯颜定为城守之计。

translations.literal: Puyanbuhua returned and with Boyan fixed a plan for defending the city.
translations.idiomatic: Puyanbuhua returned and with Zhang Boyan organized the city's defense.

sentences.zh: 后数日，道童始自南昌民家来归，遂议分门各守以备敌。

translations.literal: Several days later Daotong at last returned from a Nanchang commoner's house, and they then discussed guarding each gate separately to prepare against the enemy.
translations.idiomatic: Days later Daotong crept back from hiding in a Nanchang household, and they assigned each gate its own defenders.

sentences.zh: 三月，贼众来围城。

translations.literal: In the third month the bandit masses came to besiege the city.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month rebels besieged the city.

sentences.zh: 城中置各厢官及各巷长，昼夕坚守，众心翕然。

translations.literal: In the city they established ward officers and lane chiefs; day and night they held firm, and popular hearts were united.
translations.idiomatic: Ward officers and lane chiefs were appointed; the people held day and night, and morale held firm.

sentences.zh: 而道童素恤民，能任人，有功者必赏，无功或不加罪，故多为之用。

translations.literal: Daotong had long been compassionate to the people, could employ men well, always rewarded those with achievement and sometimes did not punish those without—therefore many served him.
translations.idiomatic: Daotong had always cared for the people, knew how to use men, rewarded merit and often overlooked failure, and so won wide loyalty.

sentences.zh: 贼围城凡两月，而民无离志。

translations.literal: The bandits besieged the city for two months in all, yet the people had no mind to leave.
translations.idiomatic: The siege lasted two months, yet the people did not waver.

sentences.zh: 道童密召死士数千人，面涂以青，额抹黄布，衣黄衣，为前锋，又别选精锐数千为中军，而募助阵者殿后。

translations.literal: Daotong secretly summoned several thousand death-defying men, their faces painted blue, foreheads smeared with yellow cloth, dressed in yellow garments as vanguard; he also separately chose several thousand elite as central army, and recruited supporters to bring up the rear.
translations.idiomatic: Daotong secretly gathered several thousand volunteers, painted their faces blue, bound yellow cloth on their foreheads, dressed them in yellow as the vanguard, chose several thousand elite troops as the center, and recruited auxiliaries for the rear.

sentences.zh: 命万户章妥因卜鲁哈歹领之。

translations.literal: He ordered the ten-thousand-household commander Zhangtuoyinbuluhadai to lead them.
translations.idiomatic: He put them under Commander Zhangtuoyinbuluhadai.

sentences.zh: 夜半，开门伏兵栅下，黎明，钲鼓大震，因奋击贼，贼惊以为神，败走。

translations.literal: At midnight they opened the gate and hid troops beneath the palisade; at dawn gongs and drums shook greatly; they then struck the bandits fiercely; the bandits in alarm thought it divine and fled in defeat.
translations.idiomatic: At midnight they opened the gates and hid troops below the palisade; at dawn drums and gongs thundered and they charged; the rebels fled in terror, thinking it supernatural.

sentences.zh: 遂乘胜捣其营，复分兵扫其餘党。

translations.literal: Riding the victory they stormed their camp and again divided troops to sweep their remaining parties.
translations.idiomatic: They pressed the victory, stormed the rebel camp, and sent detachments to mop up the remnants.

sentences.zh: 是时，章伯颜、普颜不花之功居多。

translations.literal: At this time Zhang Boyan and Puyanbuhua's achievements were the greater part.
translations.idiomatic: Most of the credit belonged to Zhang Boyan and Puyanbuhua.

sentences.zh: 伯颜寻以疾卒。

translations.literal: Boyan soon died of illness.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Boyan soon died of illness.

sentences.zh: 朝廷以道童捍城有功，加大司徒、开府，仍赐龙衣御酒。

translations.literal: The court, because Daotong had merit in defending the city, added the titles Grand Mentor and Establishing Office, and still bestowed dragon robes and imperial wine.
translations.idiomatic: The court rewarded Daotong's defense of the city with the titles Grand Mentor and Establishing Office, along with dragon robes and imperial wine.

sentences.zh: 及秋，朝廷命亦怜真班为江西行省左丞相，火你赤为左丞，同将兵来江西。

translations.literal: By autumn the court appointed Yilianzhenban as left chief councillor of the Jiangxi Branch Secretariat and Huonichi as left vice administrator, together leading troops to Jiangxi.
translations.idiomatic: That autumn the court sent Yilianzhenban as left chief councillor of Jiangxi and Huonichi as left vice administrator with troops to reinforce the province.

sentences.zh: 未几，亦怜真班卒，道童属火你赤平富、瑞二州，分镇其地。

translations.literal: Before long Yilianzhenban died; Daotong entrusted Huonichi with pacifying Fu and Rui prefectures and garrisoning the territory in divisions.
translations.idiomatic: Yilianzhenban soon died; Daotong assigned Huonichi to pacify Fu and Rui prefectures and garrison them.

sentences.zh: 适岁大旱，公私匮乏，道童乃移咨江浙行省，借米数十万石、盐数十万引，凡军民约三日人籴官米一斗，入昏钞贰贯，又三日买官盐十斤，入昏钞贰贯，民皆便之。

translations.literal: Just then the year had great drought; public and private were depleted; Daotong then sent a dispatch to the Jiang-Zhe Branch Secretariat, borrowing several hundred thousand piculs of rice and several hundred thousand yin of salt; in all soldiers and civilians roughly every three days each person bought one dou of government rice for two strings of huanchao, and every three days bought ten jin of government salt for two strings of huanchao—the people all found it convenient.
translations.idiomatic: A severe drought had emptied public and private stores; Daotong requested from the Jiang-Zhe Branch Secretariat several hundred thousand piculs of rice and salt. Every three days soldiers and civilians could buy a dou of government rice or ten jin of government salt for two strings of paper money each, to everyone's relief.

sentences.zh: 由是按堵如故，而贼亦不敢犯其境。

translations.literal: Thereby peace and order remained as before, and the bandits also did not dare invade his territory.
translations.idiomatic: Order was restored and the rebels did not dare enter his territory.

sentences.zh: 十八年夏四月，陈友谅复攻江西城。

translations.literal: In the fourth month of summer of the eighteenth year Chen Youliang again attacked the Jiangxi capital.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month of summer 1358 Chen Youliang attacked the Jiangxi capital again.

sentences.zh: 时火你赤已升平章政事，加营国公，行便宜事，任专兵柄，而素与道童不相能，且贪忍不得将士心，见城且陷，遂夜遁去。

translations.literal: At the time Huonichi had been promoted to grand councillor, added the title Duke Who Fortifies the State, acted with discretionary authority, and held sole military power; yet he had long been incompatible with Daotong and was greedy and cruel, not winning officers' and soldiers' hearts; seeing the city about to fall, he then fled by night.
translations.idiomatic: Huonichi had been promoted to grand councillor and Duke Who Fortifies the State with discretionary authority over the army; he had long been at odds with Daotong, was greedy and cruel, and had lost the troops' loyalty. Seeing the city about to fall, he fled by night.

sentences.zh: 道童亦弃城退保抚州路，欲集诸县义兵以图克复，而势已不可为。

translations.literal: Daotong also abandoned the city, withdrew to hold Fuzhou Circuit, wished to gather righteous troops from the various counties to plan recovery, but the situation could no longer be done.
translations.idiomatic: Daotong also abandoned the city and withdrew to Fuzhou, hoping to rally county militias for recovery, but the cause was already lost.

sentences.zh: 因叹曰：「我为元朝大臣，官至极品，今城陷不守，尚何面目复见人乎！

translations.literal: He therefore sighed, saying: "I am a great minister of the Yuan dynasty, my office reached the highest rank—now the city has fallen and I could not hold it—what face remains to see people again!"
translations.idiomatic: He sighed, "I am a great minister of the Yuan, risen to the highest rank. The city has fallen on my watch—what face have I left to show anyone?"

sentences.zh: 」适贼追者至，道童欲迎敌，渡水，未登岸，贼众乘之，遂为所害。

translations.literal: " Just then rebel pursuers arrived; Daotong wished to meet the enemy; crossing water, before reaching the bank, the bandit masses seized the moment and he was thereby killed.
translations.idiomatic: Rebel pursuers caught up; he tried to fight, crossed a stream, and before he reached the bank they overtook him and killed him.

sentences.zh: 事闻，赐谥忠烈。

translations.literal: When the matter was reported, he was granted the posthumous title Zhonglie.
translations.idiomatic: When word reached court, he was granted the posthumous title Loyal and Fierce.
